2609.01040.title: Causal Evidentiary Governance for High-Risk Machine Learning Systems
2609.01040.paper_summary: Machine learning systems deployed for credit, hiring, and resource distribution are increasingly subject to regulatory oversight from policies such as the EU AI Act and GDPR. Current fairness governance practices rely on observational fairness metrics, post-hoc explainability, and immutable audit logs, but provide limited support for causal attribution and efficient evidentiary verification. We introduce Causal Evidentiary Governance (CEG), a framework in which regulated institutions commit to a versioned directed acyclic graph (DAG) that partitions causal pathways into allowable and disallowed groups. The Causal Harm Rate measures prediction variation attributable to disallowed causal pathways. Each decision is accompanied by a signed Decision-Evidence Packet (DEP), cryptographically binding the prediction to a digest of the published DAG and path-specific attributions. DEP digests can be appended to a Merkle tree to enable logarithmic-cost inclusion proofs. We validate CEG through a two-layer empirical methodology using demographic summaries from four years of PMA credit supervisory data to construct 10,000 synthetic credit applicants across four strategic DAG counterfactuals. Causal Harm Rate isolates injected causal effects more clearly than demographic parity or equalized odds. Cross-model validation and ablation studies assess robustness. Evaluation on the German Credit dataset shows that harm associated with specific causal pathways can be substantially understated by associational fairness metrics. Finally, a proof-of-concept implementation demonstrates operationally plausible throughput and highlights relevant performance tradeoffs.
2609.01040.paper_summary_zh: 機器學習系統在信用、招聘和資源分配方面的應用越來越受到來自政策的監管，例如歐盟人工智慧法案和GDPR。當前的公平治理實踐依賴於觀察性公平指標、事後可解釋性和不可變的審計日誌，但對於因果歸因和高效證據驗證的支持有限。我們提出了因果證據治理（Causal Evidentiary Governance, CEG），這是一個框架，受監管機構承諾使用版本化的有向無循環圖（DAG），將因果路徑劃分為允許和不允許的組別。因果傷害率（Causal Harm Rate）衡量由不允許的因果路徑所引起的預測變異。每個決策都附有一個簽名的決策證據包（Decision-Evidence Packet, DEP），以密碼學方式將預測綁定到已發佈DAG的摘要和路徑特定的歸因。DEP摘要可以附加到默克爾樹上，以實現對數成本的包含證明。我們通過一種兩層實證方法驗證CEG，使用四年的PMA信用監管數據的人口統計摘要，構建了10,000個合成信用申請者，涵蓋四個戰略DAG反事實。因果傷害率比人口平等或均衡機會更清晰地孤立注入的因果效應。跨模型驗證和消融研究評估其穩健性。對德國信用數據集的評估顯示，與特定因果路徑相關的傷害可能被關聯公平指標大幅低估。最後，概念驗證實現展示了運營上可行的吞吐量，並突顯了相關的性能權衡。
2609.01040.author: Samah Kareem et.al.
